claims.text: Hybrid molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo exchange simulations can be used to study the thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles exhibit size-dependent thermal stability.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles have a lower onset temperature for disordering or melting than larger particles.
The lower transition temperature of smaller particles is caused by their higher surface-to-volume ratio.
As-synthesized FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles have a near-random solid-solution structure.
Nanoparticles of approximately 3 nm, 5 nm, and 10 nm can be compared using hybrid MD/MC simulated annealing.
The simulations should heat each particle from room temperature to near melting under controlled conditions.
Nanosecond-scale simulations are suitable for the proposed analysis.
Using identical interatomic potentials for all particle sizes permits a controlled size comparison.
Increasing surface-to-volume ratio enhances surface-induced disorder in smaller nanoparticles.
Smaller nanoparticles have elevated surface energy.
Elevated surface energy increases atomic mobility and disrupts local order.
Increased mobility and disrupted local order cause structural transitions to begin earlier in smaller particles.
Larger FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles or bulk samples remain stable to higher temperatures because relative surface effects are lower.
Simulation timescale and interatomic-potential limitations may affect quantitative transition temperatures.
The expected inverse relationship between particle size and transition temperature should remain qualitatively robust.
Exact transition temperatures and disordering rates require calibration against experimental data.
